sections.html:
Marion is the county seat of Grant County, on the Mississinewa River in north central Indiana. It covers about 15.8 square miles and sits at an elevation near 814 feet.

The 2020 census counted 28,310 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 28,234. The population peaked at 39,607 in 1970, a decline of about 11,000 residents that still shapes the local market.

The ZIP codes are 46952 and 46953 and the area code is 765. The city runs on a mayor-council form of government with nine council members, six by ward and three at large.

Martin Boots and David Branson each donated 30 acres in 1831 to start the town, which was incorporated as a city in 1889 and named for Revolutionary War general Francis Marion.

The Indiana gas boom of the 1880s fed rapid growth, and nearby Gas City and Matthews boomed with it. In 1888 Congress set up the Marion Branch of the National Home for Disabled Volunteer Soldiers with a $200,000 appropriation, which became today's VA presence on the southeast side. The 212 acre Marion Branch Historic District lies about 2.5 miles southeast of downtown.

The city is linked to actor James Dean and Garfield creator Jim Davis, and it bills itself as Christmas City U.S.A., with a Walkway of Lights along nearly 4 miles of the Riverwalk.

Manufacturing has been the base for generations, including automotive components, paper products, foundry goods, machinery, wire and cable. The paper plate industry began in Marion, and a General Motors stamping and tool plant opened in the 1950s.

Plant closures hit the city hard. Thomson SA closed in 2004 and TriEnda Plastics stopped production by spring 2011.

  • Indiana Wesleyan University is the largest evangelical Christian university in the Midwest and Indiana's largest private university, counting online and regional campuses. The traditional campus enrolls about 2,800 students.
  • The VA Northern Indiana Health Care System runs the Marion campus.
  • Marion General Hospital is a nationally accredited hospital with magnet status.

Sports and events add to local identity. The Marion Giants have won eight state basketball championships and play at the 7,500 seat Bill Green Athletic Arena, and the Mississinewa 1812 festival hosts what is described as the largest War of 1812 reenactment in the U.S., recalling the December 1812 battle fought about 7 miles downstream.

Agriculture surrounds the city, with corn, soybeans, hogs and tomatoes in the Corn Belt around it.

sections.h2: What does the climate do to a Marion house?
sections.html:
Marion has cold winters and hot summers. For 1991 to 2020 the average annual precipitation was 41.76 inches with 24.5 inches of snow, and the mean daily maximum is 33.0 degrees F in January and 83.8 degrees F in July.

Records run from 108 degrees F in July to minus 23 degrees F in winter. That range stresses roofs, siding, furnaces and plumbing in unheated houses.

The Mississinewa River runs through the center of Grant County, so check the flood zone if your lot is near the water.

sections.h2: How do you get around Marion?
sections.html:
Marion Municipal Airport is about three nautical miles southwest of the central business district, and the Marion Transit System runs fixed-route and demand-response buses.

Grant County is bordered by nine counties, more than any other Indiana county, so Marion sits within easy reach of several nearby markets.

sections.h2: What are Marion's rental and property rules?
sections.html:
Marion requires owners of residential rental properties, rooming houses and apartment buildings to register with the Building Department. The requirement started January 1, 2020, and applications go to Marion Building / Code Enforcement at 301 S. Branson St., phone 765-662-9931, per the city's rental registration page.

The city's 2018 Neighborhood Preservation Ordinance sets minimum standards for all buildings.

  • Foundations, roofs, gutters, windows, doors, stairs and porches must be maintained.
  • Vacant buildings must be locked and secured and can be classified as unsafe.
  • Tarps on a structure are limited to 30 days, and the owner must tell the building department first.
  • Repairs are due within 30 days of a notice, or 15 days for unsafe buildings.
  • Fines run up to $500, and each day counts as a separate offense.

Owners outside Indiana must appoint a local agent within 30 miles, with a $500 civil penalty per parcel for failing to do so. If you inherited a house in Marion from afar, this applies to you.

The Building Commissioner can order a building vacated, sealed, repaired or demolished. Orders name the responsible party, the action required and a deadline, and most can be appealed to the Marion Board of Public Works and Safety, with hearings at least 10 days after notice.

Owners get 72 hours written notice before a routine inspection. Debris from a demolition cannot stay on the lot more than three months. A buyer who purchases a damaged house as-is takes over those obligations, which is often the reason a seller with a deteriorated house prefers a cash sale.

sections.h2: When are Grant County property taxes due, and what happens to unpaid ones?
sections.html:
The Grant County Treasurer listed May 11 and November 10 as the 2026 installment dates, with bills mailed by April 15. The office is at 401 S. Adams Street, 2nd Floor, Marion, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and no longer takes payments by phone.

Unpaid taxes can lead to a tax sale. The county's 2026 sale is set for October 26, 2026, and the certified list held 672 properties. The minimum bid covers delinquent taxes, current-year taxes, penalties and costs. For certificates sold, the redemption period ends October 26, 2027, with redemption costing 110 percent of the minimum bid within six months and 115 percent later, plus certain added costs.

If your house is on that list, selling before the sale is one way to clear it, because a property is removed if the full judgment amount is paid first.

sections.h2: How is a Marion deed recorded?
sections.html:
The Grant County Recorder is at 401 S. Adams Street, 3rd Floor, phone (765) 668-6559, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Documents prepared in Indiana must include a Social Security number redaction affirmation, and card payments carry a 3.0 percent convenience fee.

Indiana law has the parties complete a sales disclosure form before the deed goes to the auditor. Your closing or title company usually manages the filing.

faqs.q: Is Marion, Indiana in Grant County?
faqs.a: Yes. Marion is the Grant County seat and the county's largest city, on the Mississinewa River.

faqs.q: Do landlords in Marion have to register rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners of residential rentals, rooming houses and apartment buildings in city limits register with the Building Department. The rule took effect January 1, 2020.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Grant County?
faqs.a: For 2026 the Treasurer listed May 11 and November 10. State law sets the installments at May 10 and November 10.

faqs.q: What happens if my Marion house is in the county tax sale?
faqs.a: Properties on the certified list can be sold at auction, but a property is removed if the full judgment amount is paid before the sale. After a sale, owners can redeem within a set period at a stated cost.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marion house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase it as-is and take on the repairs. Marion's ordinance sets deadlines and fines for violations, so deal with open notices in the sale terms.

faqs.q: Can an out-of-state owner sell a Marion house?
faqs.a: Yes. Marion's ordinance asks out-of-state rental owners to name a local agent within 30 miles, and a title company can coordinate the paperwork.
